questions.text: Which word has the soft sound of 'c' (like 's')?
questions.explanation: In 'city' the letter c sounds like s. In cat, cap and can it sounds like k.

questions.text: Which word has the soft sound of 'g' (like 'j')?
questions.explanation: In 'giant' the letter g sounds like j.

questions.text: Which word begins with the consonant cluster 'sh'?
questions.explanation: 'Ship' begins with sh. Two letters joined to make one sound make a consonant cluster.

questions.text: Which word ends with the consonant cluster 'st'?
questions.explanation: 'Dust' ends with st; stamp and stick begin with it.

questions.text: Which of these is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: A proper noun is the name of a particular person, place or thing and begins with a capital letter.

questions.text: Which of these is a common noun?
questions.explanation: A common noun names any person, place or thing and does not begin with a capital letter.

questions.text: What is the opposite of 'clean'?
questions.explanation: Opposites have totally different meanings: clean — dirty.

questions.text: What is the opposite of 'healthy'?
questions.explanation: Adding 'un' to healthy gives its opposite, unhealthy.

questions.text: How many syllables are there in 'activity' (ac-ti-vi-ty)?
questions.explanation: ac-ti-vi-ty has four parts, so four syllables.

questions.text: Which punctuation mark ends a sentence with a pause?
questions.explanation: A full stop (.) ends a sentence.

questions.text: Which word comes first in alphabetical (ABC) order?
questions.explanation: 'Activity' starts with a, which comes first in the alphabet.

questions.text: In the speech 'First Day in Class III', what is the most important class rule?
questions.explanation: The speech says the most important rule is to keep our classroom clean.

questions.text: Which of these letters is a vowel?
questions.explanation: The vowels are a, e, i, o and u. All other letters are consonants.

questions.text: Which word has a long vowel sound?
questions.explanation: In 'boat' the vowel says its own name (oa). Hit, bed and box have short vowel sounds.

questions.text: Which word has a short vowel sound?
questions.explanation: A vowel in the middle of a short word like 'cat' is usually short.

questions.text: In the poem 'Golden Sun', the sun is called the life of all ______.
questions.explanation: The poem says: 'You are the life of all things' — life on earth depends on the sun.

questions.text: Which word is a conjunction (joining word)?
questions.explanation: A conjunction joins words or sentences, like and, but, or, because.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: 'Do you want to buy a shirt ___ a pair of shoes?'
questions.explanation: 'Or' is used to give a choice between two things.

questions.text: Which pair of words are anagrams?
questions.explanation: An anagram is made by rearranging the letters of another word: break → baker.

questions.text: In 'The pencil is on the table', what is the subject?
questions.explanation: The subject is what the sentence is about: the pencil. 'Is' is the verb.

questions.text: How do we write 68 in words?
questions.explanation: 68 is sixty-eight.

questions.text: 'Intonation' means:
options: the rise and fall of the voice while speaking
questions.explanation: Intonation is the rise and fall of our voice; yes/no questions end with a rising voice.

questions.text: In 'My Happy Home', what is the name of the girl telling about her family?
questions.explanation: The text begins: 'My name is Bano. I live in a small house.'

questions.text: What pet does Bano have?
questions.explanation: Bano has a white kitten as a pet.

questions.text: According to the family rules, we should not accept eatables or gifts from:
questions.explanation: Strangers are people we don't know; we must not accept gifts or eatables from them.

questions.text: Which word is used with 'he, she and it'?
questions.explanation: 'Has' is used with he, she and it; 'have' is used with I, we, you and they.

questions.text: What is the short form (contraction) of 'I have'?
questions.explanation: I have → I've.

questions.text: What is the contraction of 'has not'?
questions.explanation: has not → hasn't.

questions.text: Which of these is a feminine noun?
questions.explanation: 'Niece' is feminine; nephew is its masculine.

questions.text: Which of these is a neuter noun (neither male nor female)?
questions.explanation: A ship is not male or female, so it is neuter gender.

questions.text: What is the feminine of 'horse'?
questions.explanation: The female of a horse is a mare.

questions.text: Which mark shows mood and emotion, as in 'Pakistan has won the match!'?
questions.explanation: An exclamation mark (!) shows strong feelings.

questions.text: How many syllables are in 'vacation' (va-ca-tion)?
questions.explanation: va-ca-tion has three syllables.

questions.text: Which companion said he had never seen anyone kinder to children than the Rasool ﷺ?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Anas (RA) said: 'I have never seen anyone act more kindly towards children than Allah's Rasool.'

questions.text: Who were the grandchildren of the Rasool ﷺ mentioned in the unit?
options: Hazrat Imam Hassan and Hazrat Imam Hussain
Hazrat Abu Bakr and Hazrat Umar
questions.explanation: The unit tells how the Rasool ﷺ picked up Hazrat Imam Hassan and Hazrat Imam Hussain when they fell.

questions.text: To whom did the Rasool ﷺ give the first fruit of the season?
questions.explanation: When the first fruit of the season was brought, he gave it to the youngest child present.

questions.text: In battles, the Rasool ﷺ ordered his followers:
options: not to kill women and children
to leave children alone in the desert
questions.explanation: Even in battle he commanded that women and children must not be killed.

questions.text: A 'Naat' is a poem that:
questions.explanation: A Naat is a poem that specially praises Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.text: Two letters joined to give one sound, like 'ch' in chair, are called a:
questions.explanation: A digraph is one sound made by two letters; a trigraph is made by three letters (tch in watch).

questions.text: Which word ends with the trigraph 'tch'?
questions.explanation: 'Catch' ends with t-c-h, three letters that make one sound.

questions.text: Which word is an adjective in 'My father bought a new house'?
questions.explanation: An adjective describes a noun: 'new' describes the house.

questions.text: Which word is a possessive adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Our' shows who owns something, as in 'Our house is new'.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the present continuous tense?
questions.explanation: The present continuous (is/am/are + -ing) shows an action going on now.

questions.text: Fill in the conjunction: 'He was holding an umbrella ___ it was raining.'
questions.explanation: He held the umbrella for a reason — because it was raining.

questions.text: The three basic elements of a story are:
options: full stop, comma and question mark
questions.explanation: Every story has a beginning, a middle and an end, along with characters, place and time.

questions.text: Where should we cross the road?
questions.explanation: The black and white lines of the zebra crossing are the safe place to cross.

questions.text: Before crossing the road, after standing at the side we first look to the:
questions.explanation: Step 1: stand at the side and look to your right; step 2: look left; step 3: look right again and cross.

questions.text: What does the red traffic light tell us?
questions.explanation: The poem 'Traffic Lights' says: red light — stop, yellow — start (get ready), green — go.

questions.text: What does the green traffic light tell us?
questions.explanation: Green means go.

questions.text: When should we get down from a school van?
questions.explanation: Keep sitting till the bus or van stops; never get down from a moving vehicle.

questions.text: Where should we walk on a busy road?
options: in the middle of the road
on the zebra crossing all the time
questions.explanation: Walk on the footpath to stay safe.

questions.text: What is the contraction of 'does not'?
questions.explanation: does not → doesn't.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: With he/she/it we use doesn't + the present form of the verb (play).

questions.text: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: We can count glasses, but we cannot count water.

questions.text: Which of these is a countable noun?
questions.explanation: Bicycles can be counted: one bicycle, two bicycles.

questions.text: 'Can' shows ability. Which sentence shows inability?
questions.explanation: 'Cannot' (can't) is used for things we are not able to do.

questions.text: Which word means 'a machine with wheels and an engine'?
questions.explanation: Cars, buses and trucks are vehicles.

questions.text: In 'The Day of Silence', what problem did Rizwan have since birth?
questions.explanation: Rizwan could not hear since birth, so he learnt sign language.

questions.text: How did Rizwan communicate with others?
questions.explanation: A doctor advised his parents to help him learn sign language.

questions.text: Why was Rizwan unhappy?
options: People treated him like a little child
questions.explanation: His parents and the villagers treated him as a little child, which made him feel unhappy.

questions.text: Who had the idea of 'The Day of Silence'?
questions.explanation: His friend Mumtaz asked his father to arrange a festival for people who could not hear.

questions.text: On 'The Day of Silence', everyone in the town wore:
questions.explanation: Everyone put earplugs in their ears for the whole day.

questions.text: What lesson does the story teach?
options: Everyone has a special talent and should be given an equal chance
Games are a waste of time
We should not go to festivals
questions.explanation: The story ends: everyone has some special talent and should be given an equal chance.

questions.text: What is the plural of 'box'?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in x, s, sh or ch add 'es': box → boxes.

questions.text: What is the plural of 'visitor'?
questions.explanation: Most nouns just add 's': visitor → visitors.

questions.text: Fill in the article: 'I saw ___ elephant yesterday.'
questions.explanation: 'An' is used before words beginning with a vowel sound (e, a, i, o, u).

questions.text: Fill in the article: 'Ahmad is ___ best boy of my class.'
questions.explanation: 'The' is used for a particular one, including with 'best'.

questions.text: Which needs 'an' because of a silent 'h'?
questions.explanation: We say 'an hour' because the h in hour is silent.

questions.text: Which word has a silent 'b'?
questions.explanation: In 'lamb' the b is not spoken.

questions.text: Which of these is an outdoor game?
questions.explanation: Games played in the playground like cricket, hockey and kabaddi are outdoor games.

questions.text: Which of these is an indoor game?
questions.explanation: Ludo is played indoors with family members.

questions.text: According to the text, sports help children to:
options: become leaders and learn the value of time
questions.explanation: The text says sports help children become leaders and teach them the value of time.

questions.text: Which activity gives energy and strength to the body, as the text says?
questions.explanation: Skipping rope is popular and gives energy and strength to the body.

questions.text: Which word begins with the consonant cluster 'cr'?
questions.explanation: Crown begins with cr; spider, space and special begin with sp.

questions.text: Which word begins with the consonant cluster 'sp'?
questions.explanation: Sparrow begins with sp.

questions.text: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is environment.

questions.text: Which of these is an action (doing) verb?
questions.explanation: Action verbs show what we can do: jump, run, write.

questions.text: Homophones sound the same but have different meanings. Choose the pair of homophones.
questions.explanation: Here and hear sound the same but are spelt differently and mean different things.

questions.text: Fill in: 'I can ___ the birds singing.'
questions.explanation: 'Hear' means to listen with the ears; 'here' means this place.

questions.text: 'Sibling' means:
questions.explanation: Your siblings are your brothers and sisters.

questions.text: Which of these is a natural resource?
questions.explanation: Air, water, land, sunlight, minerals, plants and animals are gifts of nature (natural resources).

questions.text: Why will there be a shortage of water in future, according to the text?
questions.explanation: The text warns that if we continue wasting water there will be an acute shortage.

questions.text: How can we save water while brushing our teeth?
options: Wash the car with a hose
questions.explanation: Turn off the tap while brushing teeth and washing hands.

questions.text: Which is a good way to save electricity?
options: Leave fans on in empty rooms
Keep the TV on all night
questions.explanation: Switch off extra lights and fans and use natural light.

questions.text: Paper is made of:
questions.explanation: Paper is made of wood, so using less paper means fewer trees are cut down.

questions.text: Which form of energy from the sun can help us save electricity?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is another service that can help us save electricity.

questions.text: Choose the possessive pronoun: 'The bag belongs to Hina. It is ___.'
questions.explanation: 'Hers' is a possessive pronoun that shows the bag is Hina's.

questions.text: 'My parents and I live in this house. The house is ___.'
questions.explanation: 'Ours' shows that the house belongs to us.

questions.text: In 'Arif played a match. He enjoyed it.', which word is a pronoun used for Arif?
questions.explanation: A pronoun is used in place of a noun: 'He' stands for Arif.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: 'He ___ books.'
questions.explanation: With he/she/it we use 'has'.

questions.text: Which word shows where the cat is: 'A cat is under the table'?
questions.explanation: 'Under' is a preposition: it shows the position of the cat.

questions.text: 'To make unclean' is the meaning of:
questions.explanation: To pollute means to make air, water or land dirty.

questions.text: 'Culture' means:
options: the way people live, think and behave in a society
questions.explanation: The unit defines culture as the way people live, think and behave in a society.

questions.text: According to the text, Pakistanis are known as:
options: hospitable people who take care of guests
questions.explanation: Pakistanis are hospitable people; we always take care of our guests.

questions.text: Which is a religious festival?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha are religious festivals.

questions.text: Pakistan Day (23rd March) commemorates:
questions.explanation: Pakistan Day is celebrated to commemorate the Lahore Resolution.

questions.text: Which polite expression do we use to thank someone?
questions.explanation: 'Thank you' shows gratitude; 'You're welcome' is the reply.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the simple past tense?
questions.explanation: 'Taught' is the past form of teach.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the simple future tense?
questions.explanation: We use will/shall with the first form of the verb for the future.

questions.text: 'We went to our village last Sunday' is in the:
questions.explanation: 'Went' and 'last Sunday' show the past.

questions.text: Fill in: 'Yesterday, they ___ playing cricket in the park.'
questions.explanation: With 'they' in the past we use 'were'.

questions.text: Which word has a short 'e' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Pet' has a short e sound; bee, see and tree have a long e.

questions.text: In the poem 'Our Family Picnic', what spoiled the picnic?
questions.explanation: It got rainy and dark, things blew away, mosquitoes bit them and bees attacked them.

questions.text: Which word begins with the blend 'str'?
questions.explanation: 'Street' begins with the blend str; 'quiet' and 'quick' begin with qu.

questions.text: Which word begins with 'qu'?
questions.explanation: 'Quick' begins with qu.

questions.text: A compass rose on a map is used to show:
questions.explanation: A compass rose tells directions such as North, South, East and West.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence for asking permission.
questions.explanation: 'May' is used for seeking permission.

questions.text: Which word is a preposition?
questions.explanation: Prepositions like with, in, over, from, about show the relation of a noun to other words.

questions.text: Which shows possession with an apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: We add 's to show that something belongs to someone: Majid's car.

questions.text: What is the contraction of 'I will'?
questions.explanation: I will → I'll.

questions.text: What is the contraction of 'who is'?
questions.explanation: who is → who's.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: '___ you swim?' (asking about ability)
questions.explanation: 'Can' asks about ability.

questions.text: 'It ___ rain tomorrow.' (a possibility)
questions.explanation: 'May' is used for something that is possible in the future.

questions.text: In the story, on whom did the wizard first use his new spell for perfect teeth?
questions.explanation: The wizard decided to use the spell on one of his toads.

questions.text: What did the toad love to eat after getting perfect teeth?
questions.explanation: The toad said he preferred eating candies, and he ate many sweets.

questions.text: What happened to the toad's teeth in the end?
questions.explanation: A tooth started decaying, the decay spread, and his teeth fell out.

questions.text: What lesson does the story of the toad teach?
options: Look after your teeth and don't eat too many sweets
Eat as many sweets as you like
questions.explanation: The wizard told the toad: look after your teeth, don't eat so many sweets.

questions.text: Which letter is silent in 'knife'?
questions.explanation: In knife the k is silent.

questions.text: Which letter is silent in 'write'?
questions.explanation: In write the w is silent.

questions.text: How many syllables are there in 'banana' (ba-na-na)?
questions.explanation: ba-na-na has three syllables.

questions.text: In which word is 'ed' pronounced /id/?
questions.explanation: After t or d, -ed sounds like /id/: wanted, needed.

questions.text: Which question word asks about a place?
questions.explanation: 'Where' asks about a place.

questions.text: Which question word asks about a person?
questions.explanation: 'Who' asks about a person.

questions.text: A dictionary lists words and their meanings in:
questions.explanation: A dictionary is always in alphabetical order.

questions.text: Fill in: 'Wash your hands ___ eating food.'
questions.explanation: We wash our hands before eating to keep germs away.
